headline: New law lets small inventors and businesses avoid patent office fines if they wrongly claimed a fee discount in good faith.
what_it_does: The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office charges lower patent fees to small entities and micro entities, such as small businesses and individual inventors. Before this law, anyone who falsely claimed one of these discounts faced a fine. This law says the fine does not apply if the person or business honestly believed, in good faith, that they qualified for the discount.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses and individual inventors seeking patents
who_it_affects.how: They will not be fined if they claim a reduced patent fee in good faith but turn out not to qualify.
The agency must apply a good faith exception before fining someone for a false claim of a fee discount.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 17, 2024; the summary does not give a separate effective date.
